blocks.text: A spec-driven AI workflow had grown into around 500 lines of rules, hardcoded logic and no test discipline. The core flow was small; everything around it got in the way.

On a previous team, I built quality gates (pre-commit, pre-push) and a “grill” step that checked each spec against the current codebase before implementation. Without knowing why a ticket had been blocked, it flagged the same missing backend data the team had found.
I audited the workflow against two reference implementations, removed what wasn’t pulling its weight, and introduced red/green/refactor:

items.label: Red
items.text: Acceptance criteria become behaviours and failing tests.

items.label: Green
items.text: The smallest code that makes them pass.

items.label: Refactor
items.text: Clean it up with the tests as a safety net.

blocks.text: Split it into smaller pull requests and share a short proposal first. Next step: enforce TDD with a gate instead of an instruction.
